extracted.intended_audience: news editors, social media managers, journalists, and media scholars interested in Instagram news dissemination
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and news values that determine whether news content succeeds on Instagram — a visual-first platform — and how traditional newsworthiness should be reformulated for the medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to elite/famous people
rubrics_metrics.description: News that references elites or famous people is a major driver of attention on Instagram.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Celebrity or elite mention increases likelihood of shares/likes/comments. Use famous names or recognizable figures to boost reach; absence of recognizable actors reduces insta-engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency / Instantaneity
rubrics_metrics.description: Immediacy is key; instantaneous reporting/relevance replaces traditional notions of frequency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Posts that convey up-to-the-minute information or capitalize on momentary attention windows perform better. Timeliness and being 'now' are prioritized over periodic depth; speed can trump completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Being first or offering unique content increases insta-worthiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusive photos, behind-the-scenes access, or novel angles that users cannot find elsewhere drive attention. Being unique or first to show an image/video is valuable; repackaged or widely available content is less rewarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Level of audience interaction (e.g., number and quality of comments) is a criterion for success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure by comment counts and conversations; posts that invite responses, questions, or debates increase algorithmic and social visibility. Encourage engagement through CTAs, questions, and prompts to comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viewing rating
rubrics_metrics.description: Video view counts are an important metric of news success on the platform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short video views, completion rates, and view milestones act as signals of attention. Prioritize video content optimized for quick consumption and early hold to maximize view metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual aesthetic appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Composition, color, and framing determine visual newsworthiness on Instagram.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality photography, strong composition, compelling color palettes, and intentional framing increase share-ability and attention. Visual design choices matter more than text-based prominence; poor aesthetics reduce engagement even for important stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positive content preference
rubrics_metrics.description: Instagram audiences prefer general news, human interest, and positive stories, though negative news can still gain attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize uplifting, human-centered narratives where possible; explicitly negative or politicized stories may underperform. Balance necessary negative reporting with emotionally resonant or hopeful storytelling to improve reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual stories (personal-level narratives) are favored over institutional or abstract reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame news around specific people, experiences, and personal perspectives rather than institutions or policy abstractions to increase relatability and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity-signaling
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories that affirm users' values or allow identity expression are especially shareable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content that lets users signal their beliefs, tastes, or group membership (e.g., values-affirming pieces, culturally resonant images) is more likely to be saved, shared, and displayed by users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share-ability
rubrics_metrics.description: Content that is quotable, screenshot-able, or easy to repost is more likely to spread on Instagram.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design posts with clear, bite-sized takeaways, memorable quotes, or visually framed facts that users can easily capture and share. Avoid long, dense textual explanations that don't translate to quick shares.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual and emotional reframing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: News must be reframed visually and emotionally for Instagram; the traditional inverted-pyramid plus headline approach is ineffective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate stories into strong visual hooks and emotional narratives rather than relying on headline-first text. Prioritize imagery, emotional appeal, and platform-native formats (carousel, reels, stories) over long lead paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic performance: politics vs human interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Some topics (politics) tend to underperform on Instagram relative to human-interest stories; topic fit matters for insta-worthiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect political coverage to get less engagement unless translated into strongly visual, personalized, or identity-signaling formats. Favor human interest and lifestyle angles when adapting traditionally political or policy stories.
